answer: Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. Fingerprints are counted in sparrow, which means the distribution is public, and mirror lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a kernel header, so 3962 keys running one model collapse to a single share. That is 2 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
